items.title: 0rwx – A simple model of AI usage, inspired by Unix permissions
items.reason: 0rwx proposes a four-level, Unix-permission-style label (ZER0/READ/WRITE/EXECUTE) for how much AI involvement went into a piece of work, keyed on the creator's ability to scrutinize the output. A neat framing but the only concrete artifacts are four CC0 SVG badges, no tooling or adoption signal.
key_facts: Four levels: ZER0 (HAND MADE), READ (AI INSPIRED), WRITE (AI COLLABORATION), EXECUTE (AI MADE, creator can no longer read their own work)
Only concrete deliverable is four public-domain (CC0) SVG badge logos; no scoring tool or enforcement mechanism

items.title: NariQ: BF16-level Qwen3.8-27B in a 10 GB file
items.reason: NariQ is a trellis-coded (QTIP-style) post-training quantization scheme calibrated on real coding-agent traces. Its own benchmarks show the 3-bit (10.1GB) and 2.5-bit (8.4GB) files matching or beating BF16 (53.8GB) on DeepSWE, Terminal-Bench, AIME and MGSM; 2-bit degrades sharply. Requires a llama.cpp fork, SM120-tuned, self-reported numbers.
key_facts: 3-bit NariQ (10.1GB) beats BF16 (53.8GB) on DeepSWE v1.1 (41.0 vs 39.8) and Terminal-Bench 2.1 (63.8 vs 62.6)
2.5-bit (8.4GB) stays close to BF16; 2-bit (6.8GB) drops sharply (DeepSWE 28.6 vs 39.8)
Requires nari-labs' llama.cpp fork; stock llama.cpp/Ollama/LM Studio can't load the tensor format yet
Self-reported by the authors using the Claude Code harness, not independently verified

items.title: OpenAI and Cisco introduce Shirudo
items.reason: OpenAI and Cisco's open-source Shirudo uses eBPF to apply temporary, signed 'shields' that block an exploit's specific behavior on a running Linux system while a real patch is prepared, with TPM-backed verification. Demoed live blocking a Java4Shell exploit on a running Elasticsearch process. BSD-2-Clause, concrete mechanism beyond a press release.
key_facts: Mechanism: eBPF programs ('shields') cryptographically signed and TPM-verified, loaded without restart
Codex-generated shield added an input check to Java's Base64 decoder, blocking a live Java4Shell exploit on Elasticsearch
BSD-2-Clause license, BPF programs dual BSD/GPL; GitHub repo, VM quickstart, self-guided lab

items.title: Finding faster quantum algorithms with agents and formal verification
items.reason: DeepMind used teams of Gemini 4 agents to improve known quantum algorithms, with every result formally verified in a new open-source Lean library (since the circuits can't be tested on classical or current quantum hardware). Concrete, large speedups across five problems.
key_facts: Inertial confinement fusion: 11.8x lower computing cost, qubits 5650->4338
Cytochrome P450 simulation: 2.5x improvement, qubits 481->333; light-sensitive molecule sim 8x cheaper
Grover's algorithm implementation 2.57x speedup; arcsin loading routine 290x speedup
Lean library, problem specs and verified solutions open-sourced at github.com/google-deepmind/formal-quantum-computation

items.title: RoboTrack: Point tracking for real-world robotic manipulation
items.reason: Ai2's RoboTrack: a point-tracking benchmark (307 human-annotated videos) and 15M-track synthetic training set for robotic manipulation, plus two fine-tuned tracker models and code. Trackers lose 3-6.6 AJ points moving from RoboTAP to the harder RoboTrack-Bench; the new models close part of that gap and win a real pipetting test 17/20 vs 8/20 and 5/20 for baselines.
key_facts: RoboTrack-Bench: 307 human-annotated videos, 2,522 verified point tracks; every existing tracker scores 3-6.6 AJ lower than on RoboTAP
RoboTracker (17M params) and RoboTracker-Warp (1B params) improve RoboTrack-Bench AJ from 62.6->63.4 and 63.9->66.0
Wet-lab pipetting test: RoboTracker completes 17/20 trials vs 8/20 for SAM3 masks and 5/20 for RAFT optical flow
Models, 15M-track dataset, benchmark and code released (allenai/robotrack); Warp weights are noncommercial

items.title: How to build and maintain an agentic evaluation
items.reason: A detailed, concrete methodology for building agentic evals (HF blog): worked Raman-fitting example showing a shortcut that gamed the original task, benchmark-error stats (28/89 Terminal-Bench tasks corrected, 59.4% of audited SWE-bench Verified problems had issues), and a checklist for publishing evals responsibly. Directly on Mine's always-surface eval-methodology topic.
key_facts: Worked example: unguarded raman-fitting shortcut passed all 8 synthetic tasks by guessing peak widths; fixed by adding per-peak checks
Terminal-Bench 2.1 corrected 28 of 89 tasks after user reports; harness changes alone shifted accuracy up to 29.9 points
Audit found material issues in 59.4% of 138 examined SWE-bench Verified problems; OpenAI estimated ~30% of SWE-Bench Pro tasks broken
~3,500 eval leaderboards and ~17,000 eval datasets on the Hub, roughly 16x growth in eval datasets over the past year

items.title: CrowdStrike to purchase Zscaler for $43.9 billion
items.reason: CrowdStrike acquires Zscaler for $43.9B all-stock, the largest cybersecurity deal ever (bigger than Google-Wiz). Framed explicitly around securing AI agents: Kurtz wants 'the largest AI safety and security firm' and Chaudhry calls AI agents a major new security weakness. Corporate M&A with no technical result, but the scale and the AI-agent-security rationale make it hard to skip.
key_facts: $43.9B all-stock; Zscaler holders get 1.135 CrowdStrike shares each ($260.41/share)
Largest cybersecurity M&A ever, surpassing Google's $32B Wiz deal
Zscaler CEO Chaudhry stays on, joins CrowdStrike board; ~8,000 Zscaler customers incl. half of Fortune 500
Explicit rationale: unified platform to deploy/govern AI agents and extend zero-trust to agent traffic
